before.evidence: Independently checked all three current proof steps and full Gaussian density and score suppliers. Bayes normalization gives reversed Markovness. The small-time heat expansion is locally uniform for fixed positive forward time, but the martingale proof does not integrate that remainder. Instead the exact target-time derivative of P_(v(b)-v(a))(p_a phi)/p_b is K_(u,r)(Ltilde_r phi), by the heat equation and compact-support integration by parts. The test generator has a uniform global bound on forward times >=epsilon; probability normalization bounds the derivative by that same constant. Integrating away from the diagonal then using the approximate identity limit proves the finite-time identity. Bounded conditional Fubini gives the true martingale. This independently confirms the earlier local repair ml101-b67-gaussian-kernel-integrated-identity. Singular mu and R=0 are allowed; no score at zero or unproved generic generator inference remains.

The shifted forward conditional expectation is the heat semigroup of compact smooth f composed with h; moving derivatives to that test proves the backward equation and bounded Lg. Hence every added premise of the generic martingale clause is actually verified. The reverse drift is -x/(T-u) outside the compact region and smooth with bounded derivative inside on the truncated interval. A test affine near x_star distinguishes generators on an open positive-density set.
